images.filename: Merchant Navy Memorial - plaques - Lusitania A-P.jpg
images.caption:
The right five columns of panel 11 in the pavilion of the Tower Hill Memorial, commemorating those who lost their lives in the first world war. Almost two thirds of the people listed here lost their lives when the RMS Lusitania was torpedoed on 7 May 1915.
The listings are arranged alphabetically by ship, and are listed in surname order from the bottom of the column to the top, ignoring the horizontal bands. The listing for the Lusitania begins in the third horizontal band of the middle column and continues to fill the rest of that column, the next two columns and most of the first column on panel 12.
images.alt:

images.filename: Acorn Street Boston, Massachusetts.jpg
images.caption: Acorn Street is a historic and picturesque cobblestone street located in the renowned Beacon Hill neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts, USA. This charming street has become a beloved attraction, drawing visitors from near and far. Acorn Street is characterized by its well-preserved row houses, constructed in brick and stone, which exude a timeless elegance. The street's gas lamps, quaint flower boxes, and narrow layout create a nostalgic ambiance, evoking the charm of the 19th century. Particularly during the autumn season, Acorn Street's beauty reaches new heights, as the vibrant foliage of the trees that line the street transforms into a stunning tapestry of red and orange hues. Although Acorn Street is a popular destination for tourists, its appeal extends beyond its visual splendor. The street provides a glimpse into Boston's rich history and serves as a living testament to the city's architectural heritage. Whether strolling along the cobblestones or admiring the captivating facades, a visit to Acorn Street offers a truly immersive experience in the heart of Boston's cultural tapestry.
